notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Jeremiah 47 this time. My first try fetched eight commentary pages at once, and that went over the tool's usage limit. When I tried again with just Enduring Word, the tool told me I had no calls left for this turn. So I haven't read a single page.

You asked me to report only what the sources actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written anything. Anything I gave you now would come from memory, with no page behind it.

In your next message, I'll fetch the pages one or two at a time so I stay under the limit. I'd go in this order:

1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:**
   - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/jeremiah-47/
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/jeremiah/47.htm (Gill)
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/jeremiah/47.htm (Ellicott)
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/jeremiah/47.htm (Pulpit Commentary)
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/jeremiah/47.htm (Matthew Henry)
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/barnes/jeremiah/47.htm (Barnes)
   - preceptaustin.org's Jeremiah 47 page
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** I'd search the Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan, Pentecostal and Lutheran sites for this chapter. It's a short oracle against a foreign nation, so the traditions may not really disagree on it. If they don't, I'll say so rather than invent a debate.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes on verses 1, 4 and 5, plus searches of bibleodyssey.org and the Catholic and Orthodox sites. Those notes would probably cover which Pharaoh struck Gaza, what "Caphtor" refers to and the textual question in verse 5. I'll only include popular modern teaching (prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace) if a site actually discusses this chapter.

Just reply "continue" and I'll start, with the URL after every point.
